title: Kubric: A Scalable Dataset Generator
abstract: Source summary: the official repository describes a modular synthetic multi-object video generator built around PyBullet and Blender, with instance segmentation, depth, optical-flow annotations, physics simulation, and controllable train/test compositional splits.

title: BlenderProc
abstract: Source summary: the official repository describes a procedural Blender pipeline with physics and collision checking, material/light/camera randomization, RGB/stereo/depth/normal/segmentation rendering, optical-flow rendering, and COCO/BOP writing.

title: Objaverse: A Universe of Annotated 3D Objects
abstract: Source summary: Objaverse 1.0 officially advertises 800K+ annotated 3D objects and 44K+ animated objects, including rigged characters and varied visual styles. Individual asset terms are metadata-dependent; dataset availability must not be mistaken for one homogeneous redistributable asset license.
query: Objaverse official GitHub dataset license Google Scanned Objects official dataset license

title: Tracking through Containers and Occluders in the Wild
abstract: Source summary: TCOW is an official causal video object-permanence/segmentation system. Its repository trains a 30-frame 320x240 Transformer with causal attention on a Kubric-derived dataset and provides Kubric generation templates with X-ray annotations. The documented example used two RTX A6000 GPUs and about 38 GB VRAM per GPU at batch size one.
query: causal video occlusion tracking amodal segmentation memory reappearance TCOW CoTracker TAPIR

title: TAPIR: Tracking Any Point with Per-Frame Initialization and Temporal Refinement
abstract: Source summary: the official TAP repository supplies TAPIR/BootsTAPIR checkpoints, causal online inference, Kubric training instructions and TAP-Vid evaluation. It describes temporal consistency across spatial transformations, corruptions and query choices as the self-supervised signal used by BootsTAP.

title: CoTracker3: Simpler and Better Point Tracking by Pseudo-Labelling Real Videos
abstract: Source summary: the official CoTracker3 repository releases offline and online checkpoints, pseudolabelling code, and Kubric-only baseline checkpoints. It is point tracking with a visibility output, not an instance-level amodal or identity model; a GPU is strongly recommended for local use.

title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
abstract: Source summary: the official SAM 2 code exposes a video predictor with image encoder, memory attention and memory encoder. Its SA-V release contains 51K videos and 643K masklets under CC BY 4.0, but these are modal masklets rather than geometric amodal labels.

title: Segment Anything, Even Occluded
abstract: Source summary: SAMEO adapts a SAM-family mask decoder to take front-end detector boxes and predict amodal masks. Its project page reports Amodal-LVIS, a synthetic 300K-image extension derived from modal LVIS/LVVIS, and emphasizes detector-decoder modularity.

title: SyDog-Video: A Synthetic Dog Video Dataset for Temporal Pose Estimation
abstract: Source summary: the official dataset page documents 500 synthetic 175-frame dog videos per version, with 2D boxes, 33 keypoints and segmentation maps. It offers multiple visual-condition variants, but does not document amodal masks, depth, frontmost-object labels or identity/reappearance targets.

title: Cosmos Transfer Sim2Real for Robotics Navigation Tasks
abstract: Source summary: NVIDIA documents video-to-video sim-to-real augmentation using RGB plus segmentation control and copying source labels after generation. The example sets segmentation control weight to 1.0 and asserts label reuse. Its 8×H100, two-stage 100-epoch specification is for downstream X-Mobility world-model/action-policy training, not a documented cost for the Transfer generator itself.
